title: Reports
summary: The reports hub: one long page that reads the café's figures for the dates (and the place) you choose. This entry covers the top of the page: the dates and place, printing, the period at a glance, what the period says, where the money went, the jump links and the links to the other reports. The report sections below it have their own entries (Profit, Sales, Buying and stock, People, Checks).

See every part of the page and every report link; the Watch list link only when the owner allows it.
who.cannot: Post the journals the old app never wrote (the page says "Only the owner can post them.").

who.cannot: See what staff cost (the Salaries (6100) table needs payroll.view); see the Watch list.

who.can: See every part of the page, the staff hours with what staff cost, the profit, the exceptions and the customers.
who.cannot: See the Watch list; post the old app's journals.

who.can: The same as the accountant: read every part.
who.cannot: Change anything; see the Watch list.

who.can: Open the page and read sales, buying, stock, losses and the checks.
who.cannot: See the Profit part, the period's figures at a glance, where each 1,000 IQD went, Exceptions, Staff, Customers and loyalty, or the links to Cash ahead and Balance sheet and cash flow.
Open Reports: they are sent to their own first screen (the till).
Open Reports: they are sent to Production.
Open Reports: they are sent to the count.

get_there: Menu → Accountant → Reports (for some people it sits under More). It is the first screen for the accountant and the auditor. Also: the Dashboard's figures open it; Sales analysis and the week and month pages link back to it.
before: Nothing has to be set up: every part reads what is already recorded. Parts with nothing in the dates say so.
The profit figures come from published journals only: a draft journal is not counted.

parts.name: Heading
parts.shows: "Reports", and " · {place}" when the page is read for one place. Beside it: the Print or save as PDF button, and the line "{from} to {to} · from the ledger · every journal line (CSV)".

controls.label: Print or save as PDF
controls.does: Opens the browser's print window for the page as it stands. Choose a printer, or Save as PDF. The paper copy leaves out the menu, the forms, the jump links and the buttons, and starts with a heading: "{business} · Reports · {from} to {to} · {place} · As of {date and time}".
controls.rules: Arabic and Kurdish print right to left. Open the parts you want (for example Do the books tie?) before printing: closed parts print closed.

controls.label: every journal line (CSV)
controls.does: Downloads a spreadsheet file journal-lines_{from}_{to}.csv: every published journal line in the dates (journal no., when, day, account, account name, debit, credit, narration, memo, source, reference, posted by, reverses journal no.).
controls.rules: Always the whole café, whatever place is chosen.

parts.name: Dates and place
parts.shows: A small form with the dates and, for people who work everywhere when the café has more than one place, the place. Under it, when a place is read: "Read for {place}. These stay the whole café's: Do the books tie?, Payable Ageing, Product Margin by Channel, and the customers with the points they hold."

controls.label: From
controls.does: The first day of the dates.
controls.rules: A date. Empty or not a date: the first day of this month (by the café's clock).

controls.label: To
controls.does: The last day of the dates.
controls.rules: A date. Empty or not a date: today. From must be on or before To, or the page cannot be loaded (see States).

controls.label: Place
controls.does: Chooses the place the reports are read for: The whole café, or one of the café's places.
controls.rules: Shown only to people who work everywhere, when the café has more than one place. Default: The whole café. Someone who works at one place always reads their own place and sees no list.
controls.who: Only people not tied to one place.

controls.label: Show
controls.does: Reloads the page for the dates and place chosen.

controls.label: This month
controls.does: Shows the first of this month to today, keeping the place.

controls.label: Last month
controls.does: Shows all of last month, keeping the place.

controls.label: This year
controls.does: Shows 1 January to today, keeping the place.

parts.name: The period at a glance
parts.shows: Four tiles, each set against the days just before, as many (for 1 to 30 September: 2 to 31 August). Only for people who see profit, and only when From is on or before To. Net revenue: the P&L's net revenue (4000 Sales less 4100 discounts and 4200 refunds); its line says "{pct}% more than the {n} day(s) before", "{pct}% less than the {n} day(s) before" or "About as the {n} day(s) before" (within 5% either way is "about as"). Gross profit after waste & fees: net revenue less everything in cost of sales (recipe cost of goods, price differences on deliveries, platform commission and fees, waste, count differences); with "{pct}% of net revenue" and the change in that share in points: "{n} point(s) more than the {days} day(s) before", "{n} point(s) less than the {days} day(s) before" (less than one point either way is "About as"). Net profit (or Net loss, in red): what is left after the operating expenses too; with its share of net revenue and its change in points. Losses: everything lost or given away in the dates that was not reversed (the Losses section's total), with its share of net revenue.

controls.label: Net revenue
controls.does: Jumps to the Profit & Loss.

controls.label: Gross profit after waste & fees
controls.does: Jumps to the Profit & Loss.

controls.label: Net profit
controls.does: Jumps to the Profit & Loss. Reads "Net loss" when the period lost money.

controls.label: Losses
controls.does: Jumps to the Losses section.

parts.name: What the period says
parts.shows: The figures in sentences, each with a mark (✓ good, ▲ up, ▼ down, ● as before, ! look at this) and a link to where to act. Which sentences appear depends on the figures: see Messages. The first line is always the books check.

controls.label: (each sentence)
controls.does: Opens where to act on it: Do the books tie?, the Profit & Loss, the sales analysis by date, the largest expense's journal lines, Delivery platforms (/platforms), Losses, Payable Ageing or Uncosted Sales.

parts.name: Where each 1,000 IQD of net revenue went
parts.shows: One bar split into parts, for people who see profit, when there was net revenue. Each part says how many dinars of every 1,000 IQD of net revenue went to it, and "{amount} in all". What was sold cost: 5000 (the recipes' cost of goods). Delivery platforms: 5100 and 5200 (commission and fees). Waste and stock differences: the rest of cost of sales (waste, preparation loss, count differences, price differences on deliveries). Staff: 6100 Salaries and 6110 Staff meals. Rent and running costs: every other expense. Last: Kept as profit (or The period's loss). Under it: "From the P&L: what was sold cost is the recipes' cost of goods; waste and stock differences are waste, preparation loss, count differences and price differences on deliveries; the staff are their pay and their meals."

parts.name: Parts of the reports (jump links)
parts.shows: Links to each section, in groups. Profit: Profit & Loss, Profit & Loss by place. Sales: Sales by Channel, Product Margin by Channel, Sizes and add-ons, Sales by payment method, Dollars, Customers and loyalty. Buying and stock: Purchasing, Payable Ageing, Production, Losses. People: Staff. Checks: Do the books tie?, Uncosted Sales, Exceptions. Groups and links you may not see are left out. Not printed.

controls.label: (each section name)
controls.does: Scrolls the page to that section.

parts.name: The other reports
parts.shows: A row of links to the reports on their own pages. Each person's most opened come first: every time you open one of them it is counted for you, and once a report has been opened 3 times or more it moves ahead of those opened less (most opened first; the rest keep their usual order). When the order has changed, the row starts with "The ones you open most, first:". Nobody arranges them by hand. Stock value on a day and Balance sheet and cash flow are not counted, so they never move up.

controls.label: Sales analysis: by hour, day, product, person, payment… →
controls.does: Opens Sales analysis for the same dates (and place).

controls.label: The week at a glance →
controls.does: Opens the week ending on To (today at most), for the same place.

controls.label: The month at a glance →
controls.does: Opens the month of To (this month at most), for the same place.

controls.label: Price watch: what came in dearer →
controls.does: Opens Price watch (always the last 30 days, whole café).

controls.label: Menu matrix: what to keep, reprice, show more or drop →
controls.does: Opens Menu matrix for the same place.

controls.label: Staffed when busy? Orders an hour against who was on the clock →
controls.does: Opens the staffing report for the same place.
controls.who: Those who keep the staff, their hours or their pay (staff.manage, attendance.edit or payroll.view).

controls.label: Waste by recipe: made, sold and thrown away →
controls.does: Opens the waste report for the same place.

controls.label: Stock value on a day →
controls.does: Opens the stock's value at the end of To, for the same place.

controls.label: Cash ahead: the next 30 days of the bank and the safe →
controls.does: Opens Cash ahead.

controls.label: Balance sheet and cash flow →
controls.does: Opens the statements for the same dates.

controls.label: Watch list: patterns worth a look →
controls.does: Opens the Watch list.
controls.who: The owner; the general manager only when the owner allows it.

parts.shows: "Also:" and links to other screens with figures.

states.looks: The first of this month to today, for the whole café (or your place, if you work at one).

The heading ends " · {place}", the note "Read for {place}…" shows, and the sections are that place's, except Do the books tie?, Payable Ageing, Product Margin by Channel and the customers' points, which stay the whole café's.
No tiles, no "Where each 1,000 IQD…" bar, no Profit part; What the period says shows only the books check and the losses, supplier and uncosted lines.

states.state: No net revenue in the dates
states.looks: The tiles show 0; the bar of where the money went is not shown; the sentences about revenue and profit are not shown.
The page cannot be loaded: "This screen could not be loaded" with a Try again button. Change the dates in the address, or open Reports again from the menu.

states.state: The ones you open most moved up
states.looks: The report links start with "The ones you open most, first:" and the reports you open most lead the row.
The print heading at the top; no menu, form, jump links or buttons.

messages.text: {n} reconciliation difference(s): look into them before trusting these figures.
messages.when: One or more checks under Do the books tie? do not tie.
messages.do: Open it (the sentence links there) and look into each difference before you rely on the figures.

messages.text: The books tie: every record agrees with its account.
messages.when: Every check under Do the books tie? ties.

messages.text: Net revenue was {pct}% more than in the {n} day(s) before.
messages.when: Net revenue rose 5% or more against the same number of days before. Under it: "{now} against {before}."
messages.do: The link opens the sales analysis by date to see which days did it.

messages.text: Net revenue was {pct}% less than in the {n} day(s) before.
messages.when: Net revenue fell 5% or more. Under it: "{now} against {before}."
messages.do: Open the sales analysis by date to find the weak days, then look at the week and month pages.

messages.text: Net revenue was about as in the {n} day(s) before.
messages.when: Within 5% either way.

messages.text: Net revenue was {amount}; the {n} day(s) before had none to compare with.
messages.when: The days before had no net revenue.

messages.text: You kept {pct}% of net revenue after the cost of sales.
messages.when: There was net revenue. Under it: "{pct}% in the {n} day(s) before." Marked ▼ when the share fell a point or more, ▲ when it rose.
messages.do: If it fell, look at Product Margin by Channel and Losses: costs, prices or waste moved.

messages.text: After every expense, the period made {amount}: {pct}% of net revenue.
messages.when: Net profit is zero or more.

messages.text: After every expense, the period lost {amount}.
messages.when: Net loss.
messages.do: Open the Profit & Loss and look at the largest expenses and the cost of sales.

messages.text: {account} was the largest expense: {amount}, {pct}% of net revenue.
messages.when: There was at least one operating expense.
messages.do: The link opens that account's journal lines for the dates.

messages.text: The delivery platforms' commission and fees came to {amount}: {pct}% of net revenue.
messages.when: Platform commission and fees (5100, 5200) are 1% of net revenue or more.
messages.do: The link opens Delivery platforms; check the platforms' prices cover their fees.

messages.text: Losses came to {amount}, {pct}% of net sales.
messages.when: Anything was lost or given away in the dates (not reversed) and there were net sales. Under it: "The largest kind: {kind}, {amount}."
messages.do: Open Losses to see what, where and who.

messages.text: Losses came to {amount}.
messages.when: As above, with no net sales.

messages.text: {amount} owed to suppliers is past due, {old} of it by more than 30 days.
messages.when: Unpaid bills are past their due date, some by more than 30 days (today, whole café).
messages.do: Open Payable Ageing and pay the oldest first on Vendors.

messages.text: {amount} owed to suppliers is past due.
messages.when: Unpaid bills are past due, none by more than 30 days.

messages.text: Sales of {amount} were costed at nothing: their profit is overstated until what they use has a cost.
messages.when: Some sales in the dates went out with no cost, or part of it missing.
messages.do: Open Uncosted Sales and give the products their recipes or the items their cost.

messages.text: Read for {place}. These stay the whole café's: Do the books tie?, Payable Ageing, Product Margin by Channel, and the customers with the points they hold.
messages.when: The page is read for one place.
messages.do: Nothing; choose The whole café to see everything together.

messages.text: This screen could not be loaded
messages.when: A figure could not be read, for example when From is after To. It is followed by "The information could not be read from the database, so nothing is shown rather than something incomplete. Nothing has been changed." and "If it keeps happening, tell the owner, and quote reference {ref}." (or "If it keeps happening, tell the owner.").
messages.do: Press Try again; if the dates are the wrong way round, open Reports from the menu and choose them again.

messages.text: Sign in to continue
messages.when: A CSV link was opened after the sign-in ran out (shown as plain text in the browser).
messages.do: Sign in again and press the link again.

messages.text: You do not have permission to see this report
messages.when: A CSV the database will not give you (shown as plain text).

skipped_messages: note_report_visit: "Sign in again", "That is not one of the reports": counting a visit fails silently; nothing is shown.

report_losses, report_dollars and the other reports' "Choose the dates, the first before the last": the page shows "This screen could not be loaded" instead (the database's words appear only on a developer's machine).
report_place "Choose one of the café's places" / "You work at {1}, not at {2}": the hub only sends places from its own list, and a person at one place is always read for their place.
export "Unknown report": no link on this page sends an unknown report.

what_if.case: The figures look wrong
what_if.do: Check the first sentence of What the period says: if the books do not tie, open Do the books tie? and fix the differences first.

what_if.case: You want last month's report on paper
what_if.do: Press Last month, open the parts you want, then Print or save as PDF.

what_if.case: You want one branch only
what_if.do: Choose it in Place and press Show. Remember the four parts named in the note stay the whole café's.

what_if.case: A report you use a lot is at the end of the row
what_if.do: Just keep using it: from its third opening it moves ahead of those you open less.

tips: Every tile, sentence and many numbers are links: tap a number to see what is behind it.
The days compared are always as many as you chose, just before them: choose a whole month to compare with the month before only when both have the same number of days.
The CSV files open in Excel or Google Sheets.

title: Reports — Profit
summary: The profit and loss for the dates, from the published journals, and, when the whole café is read and it has more than one place, each place's profit and loss side by side.

who.can: See both tables and download them.

get_there: Reports → the Profit links in the jump links, or the tiles at the top.
before: Only published journals count: drafts on the Journal register are left out until published.

parts.name: Profit & Loss
parts.shows: Heading "Profit & Loss" (or "Profit & Loss at {place}"), and "Published journal lines, {from} to {to} · CSV". Income: each revenue account with an amount (4000 Sales, 4100 discounts and 4200 refunds show negative, in red), then Net revenue. Cost of sales: each account in brackets (5000 cost of goods, purchase price differences, 5100/5200 platform commission and fees, 5300 waste, 5310 preparation loss, count differences), then Gross profit after waste & fees = net revenue less cost of sales. Operating expenses: each account in brackets (salaries, staff meals, rent, utilities, complimentary items, samples…). Last: Net profit (or Net loss, in red) = gross profit less operating expenses. Accounts with nothing in the dates are not listed. A year-end close is left out.

controls.label: (each account line, e.g. "4000 Sales")
controls.does: Opens the Journal register filtered to that account and the dates: the journal lines that make the amount.

controls.label: CSV
controls.does: Downloads profit-and-loss_{from}_{to}.csv (code, account, section, amount) for the same dates and place.

parts.name: Profit & Loss by place
parts.shows: Only when the whole café is read, the café has more than one place, and you see profit. One column per place, a Shared column, and Café total. The same groups and totals as above; "—" where a place has nothing. The note explains: "Each line is at the place of its record: a sale at the branch that sold it, a loss where the stock was, an expense where it was recorded. A platform's payout is shared out by the branch of each order, a payroll by where each person works. Shared: what belongs to no one place, such as the bank's card fees and journals by hand."

controls.label: (each account line)
controls.does: Opens that account's journal lines for the dates (all places).

controls.label: CSV
controls.does: Downloads profit-and-loss-by-place_{from}_{to}.csv (code, account, section, place, amount; "shared" for no place).

states.looks: The last line reads Net loss and the amount is red.
The heading reads "Profit & Loss at {place}"; Profit & Loss by place is not shown.
Only the headings and totals of 0.

what_if.case: Net revenue here and the till's sales differ
what_if.do: Net revenue is sales less discounts and refunds, with a refund on the day it was made. Check Do the books tie? (the Sales check) and the Sales by Channel note.

what_if.case: An expense is missing
what_if.do: It may be a draft journal or recorded with another date: look on the Journal register or Expenses.

what_if.case: Gross profit is much lower than the sales margin
what_if.do: Gross profit also takes off waste, count differences, price differences on deliveries and platform fees: look at Losses and the cost-of-sales lines.

tips: Gross profit after waste & fees is not the same as the Sales margin in Sales by Channel: the margin is before waste, counts and fees.

title: Reports — Sales
summary: What was sold in the dates: by part of the menu, by channel, the margin of every product today, sizes and add-ons, the ways customers paid, dollars taken and exchanged, and customers with their points.

who.role: owner, general_manager, branch_manager, accountant, auditor, purchasing
who.can: See every section here.

get_there: Reports → Sales in the jump links.

parts.name: Café and bakery
parts.shows: Only when the menu is split into parts (Settings, menu sections) and the dates are a year or less. One row per part of the menu, and "No section" for categories in none. Sales: sales after discounts, less what refunds gave back. Share of sales: its share of all, with a bar. Cost: what those sales used. Profit: sales less cost. Margin: profit as a % of sales. Note: "Sales after discounts, less what refunds gave back; the cost is what those sales used. Rent, wages and other costs the parts share are in the profit and loss." No sales: "No sales in these dates."

parts.name: Sales by Channel
parts.shows: "Sales {from} to {to}, voids excluded; refunds on the day they were made". A bar chart "Net sales by channel", each bar with "{share}% of net sales · margin {kept}%". A table: Channel, Orders, Sales (before refunds), Refunds (in brackets), Net sales = sales less refunds, Sales margin = net sales less the recipe cost of what was sold (the cost of what went back on the shelf taken off). All channels row. Note: "Net sales are what the P&L shows as net revenue for the same dates (4000 less 4100 and 4200). The sales margin is net sales less the recipe cost of what was sold; the P&L's gross profit also takes off waste, count differences, purchase price differences and platform fees."

controls.label: (the Orders number of a channel)
controls.does: Opens Orders for the same dates and that channel.

parts.name: Product Margin by Channel
parts.shows: "Today's prices and today's costs, costed exactly as a sale posts them". Every size of every product on every channel in use: Product (— size), Channel, Price, Cost ("unknown" when it has no cost), Margin = price less cost (red when negative), % = margin ÷ price. Not affected by the dates or the place chosen. Empty: "Add products with recipes and prices to see their margins."

parts.name: Sizes and add-ons
parts.shows: "Sold {from} to {to}, at the prices and costs of each sale; voids left out". Sizes (only products sold in more than one size): Product, Size, Qty, Net sales, Cost, Margin, %. Add-ons: Group, Add-on, Qty, On lines, Of the lines offered it (on lines ÷ lines of products that offer it today), Net sales, Cost, Margin. Note: "A size's figures leave out its add-ons, which are counted on their own, each with its share of the line's discount. Refunds are not taken off here: Sales by Channel has them. How often an add-on is taken is out of the lines of the products that offer it today." Empty: "No product was sold in more than one size, and no add-on was taken, in these dates."

parts.name: Sales by payment method
parts.shows: A bar chart "Net sales by payment method" ("{share}% of net sales"). Table by Paid by (Cash, Card, Platform-paid, Other way to pay): Sales (how many; "{n} paid two ways" under it), Takings, Refunds, Net = takings less refunds, Change given; All payments row. Note: "A sale paid part in cash and part by card counts under each, for the part it paid. Cash is what the sale kept: the change went back to the customer. The net matches the sales by channel." When the café has its own ways to pay, a second table by Way to pay (" · out of use" for one no longer used): Sales, Takings, Refunds, Net and, for the whole café only, Moved out, Fees and "In its account on {day}". Its note (whole café): "The café's own ways to pay, each with its own account: what it took, what refunds gave back by it, what was moved out of its account in the dates and the fees the bank or the app kept, and what the account held at the end. Money is moved on Sales → Ways to Pay." (one place): "The café's own ways to pay, at this place: what each took, and what refunds gave back by it. Their accounts are the café's: see them for all places." Empty: "No sales in these dates."

parts.name: Dollars
parts.shows: "Taken, counted and exchanged {from} to {to}; held now". A sentence: "{sales} sale(s) paid in dollars: {usd}, taken at {value}; they paid {paid}, and {change} went back as change in dinars." (or "No sale was paid in dollars in these dates."). By rate: Dinars a dollar, Sales, Dollars, Taken at. Exchanges: When, From, Into (the till, the safe, the bank), Dollars, Taken at, Dinars received, Difference (red in brackets when less was received). Drawer counts: Session, Branch, Should have held, Counted ("Not counted"), Difference. Last line: "Exchange differences {exchanges} (6950) · dollars counted over or short {counts} (6300) · held now: the safe {safe}" and, for each till, "{place}'s till: {usd} (taken at {amount})".

controls.label: (a session number)
controls.does: Opens that drawer session.

parts.name: Customers and loyalty
parts.shows: For people who see customers. "Points earned and spent {from} to {to}, and who bought the most". "Points earned: {n}", "Rewards taken: {n}, {amount} off", "Taken back on voids and refunds: {n}; given back: {m}", "By hand: {plus} given, {minus} taken", "Customers hold {n} points now, worth {amount} in rewards" (always the whole café), "{n} customers, {m} new in these dates", "Their sales: {n}, {amount}". Note: "A reward is a discount on 4100, like any other: the points are no liability in the books, only what customers hold here." Table of top customers: Customer, Orders, Bought, Points.

controls.label: (a customer's name)
controls.does: Opens that customer.

states.looks: "No sales in these dates." in Sales by Channel, payment method and Café and bakery.
Every section is that place's except Product Margin by Channel and the points customers hold now; the ways to pay show no account columns.

what_if.case: A product's margin is red
what_if.do: Its cost is above its price on that channel: change the price or the recipe on Products & Recipes.

what_if.case: Cost shows "unknown"
what_if.do: The product has no recipe, or an ingredient has no cost yet: give it a recipe, or record a delivery or opening stock for the item.

what_if.case: A dollar exchange shows a red difference
what_if.do: Less was received than the dollars were taken at; it goes to 6950. Check the rate used at the till.

tips: Sales by Channel's Net sales equals the P&L's Net revenue for the same dates; if not, look at Do the books tie?.

title: Reports — Buying and stock
summary: What was ordered, delivered, returned and credited in the dates; what is owed to suppliers today and how late; the batches made and what became of them; and everything lost or given away.

who.role: owner, general_manager, branch_manager, accountant, auditor, purchasing
who.can: See every section here.

get_there: Reports → Buying and stock in the jump links.

parts.name: Purchasing
parts.shows: "Orders, prices, returns and credits, {from} to {to}". Orders made in the dates: Order, Supplier, Stage (Draft, Approved, Sent, Partly received, Received, Closed, Cancelled), Ordered, Received; or "No purchase order was made in these dates.". "{n} order(s) open, waiting for goods: {list}". "Prices that changed from the supplier's delivery before": Delivery, Supplier, Item, Before, Now ("{cost} a {unit}"), Change (red when dearer). "Returns to suppliers": No., Supplier, Delivery, Why, Owed back, Stock value, How ("Off the delivery's bill", "Credit {no} on the account", "On the account"). Then "What came in, by supplier": Supplier, Deliveries, Received, Sent back, Credited for price, Net = received less sent back less price credits, Billed; All row. "What came in, by item": Item, Came in, Cost of one (received ÷ quantity), Received, Sent back, Net. title: Reports — Checks
summary: Whether the books tie (every record against its account), the stock the old app never journaled, sales that went out with no cost, and the exceptions: voids, refunds, discounts, cancelled bills, items taken off bills and wrong PINs, by person.

See everything.
See Do the books tie? and Uncosted Sales.

parts.name: Do the books tie?
parts.shows: "Each subledger against its control account, as at the end of {to} · CSV". Always the whole café. Folded to one line when all tie: "Ties" mark and "Every subledger agrees with its control account."; opened by itself when one does not: "Does not tie" mark and "{n} of {total} checks do not tie". The table: Check, Subledger (what the records add up to), Ledger (what the account holds), Difference = subledger less ledger (red when not 0). The checks: Stock ledger vs Inventory (1200); Unpaid bills vs Accounts payable (2000); Unbilled receipts vs Goods received not invoiced (2050); Sales recorded vs net revenue in the ledger (4000 less 4100 and 4200); Card takings not yet settled vs Card clearing (1010); Orders the platforms owe vs Receivable from platforms (1100); What the drawers should hold vs Cash in the till (1000); Cash moved in and out of the safe vs Safe (1005); Dollars held, at what they were taken at, vs Cash in dollars (1001 and 1006); Salaries owed vs Salaries payable (2100); Advances not yet taken back vs Employee advances (1300); Stock on its way between places vs Stock in transit (1210); Prepaid expenses still to come vs Prepaid expenses (1400); and Every record has its one journal, and every automatic journal its record (a count of records, not money: "{n} record(s)" or "none"). When records are wrong: "Records to look into": When, Record (Sale, Void, Refund, Delivery, Delivery correction, Bill, Payment, Expense, Stock, Stock count, Cash moved, Drawer session, Dollars, Return to a supplier, Supplier's credit, Card settlement, Platform statement, Transfer, Journal), What is wrong.

controls.label: (the summary line)
controls.does: Opens or folds the table of checks.

controls.label: (a Subledger amount)
controls.does: Opens the records behind it: Inventory, Vendors, Purchasing, Orders (this month to To), Sales (card or safe), Platforms, Drawer sessions or Transfers.

controls.label: (a Ledger amount)
controls.does: Opens the account's journal lines from the first of To's month to To.

controls.does: Jumps to Records to look into.

controls.label: (a record in Records to look into)
controls.does: Opens where that record is kept (Orders for that day, Purchasing, Vendors, Expenses, Inventory, Count, Sales, the drawer session, Platforms, Transfers or the Journal register for that day).

parts.name: Stock the old app never journaled
parts.shows: Only when such records exist. "These records moved stock before the upgrade but have no journal, so they show above as an Inventory difference. Each would post the entry the new app writes for the same record, dated when it happened. Post them only if the records are real." Table: When, Record (Opening stock, Goods received, Count variance, Waste, Stock correction, and its description), Journal it would post (e.g. "1200 Dr 50,000 · 2050 Cr 50,000"), Amount; "{n} record(s)" and the total.

controls.label: Why they are being posted (for the audit trail)
controls.does: The reason kept on the audit trail.

controls.label: Post these {n} journal(s)
controls.does: Posts one journal for each record, oldest first, each dated when its record happened, its narration ending "(the old app never journaled it)". Shows "Posting…" while it works.
controls.rules: Disabled until a reason is typed. All or nothing: if one cannot be posted, none is.
controls.who: Owner only. Others see "Only the owner can post them."
controls.after: The books: each journal debits/credits as shown (Inventory 1200 against GRNI 2050, waste, count variance or the opening balance), so the Inventory difference above shrinks. Stock itself does not move (it already did). The journals appear on the Journal register; the audit trail records who posted how many, the total and the reason.

parts.name: Uncosted Sales
parts.shows: "Sales {from} to {to} with no cost, or part of it missing". A sale's cost is understated when a product has no recipe (and was not marked as using no stock), or an ingredient was used before it had any cost. Table: When, Products, Channel, Net sales, Cost recorded, Why. Under it the warning and how to fix it. None: "All good" and "Every sale in these dates carries its cost."

parts.name: Exceptions
parts.shows: For people with audit.view. "Voids, refunds, discounts, cancelled bills, items taken off bills and wrong PINs, {from} to {to} · CSV". By person ("No one signed in" when nobody was): Void, Refund, Discount, Bill cancelled, Printed bill reduced, Items taken off a bill, Wrong PIN (how many of each), Money involved, For review (in warning colour). The people with most to review come first. Then every one: When, What ("review" badge), Who, Amount, Why, Approved by, About. A row is for review when it is a void or refund nobody else approved, a wrong PIN, or a discount over the cap given before discounts were checked; the mark stays, it tells you what to look at. None: "All good" and "Nothing was voided, refunded, discounted, cancelled or taken off a bill in these dates."

parts.name: The analysis
parts.shows: Heading "By {first}" or "By {first}, then by {second}", and "{from} to {to} · CSV". For Hour, Day of the week or Date with no second way (and not Payment): a column chart "Net sales" — every hour from the first to the last sold in, every weekday Saturday to Friday, or every day of the dates (two months at most); each column with "{n} order(s)"; a line "Average: {amount} an hour sold in" or "Average: {amount} a day sold in" (the average of those with sales). The table, by lines sold (most ways): Orders, Items, Sold for (before the discount, add-ons in), Discount, Net = sold for less discount, Cost (what it used, at the cost it was sold at), Margin = net less cost, Given back (what refunds gave back since, whenever made), Kept = net less given back, Margin kept = kept less (cost less the cost refunds put back). By Add-on: Times taken, Items, Sold for, Discount, Net, Cost, Margin (refunds not taken off). By Payment: Sales, Paid, Given back, Kept. A thin bar beside Net (or Paid) shows its size against the largest. Hours, days and dates keep their order; the other ways put the largest first. Last row: All. An order is counted once per row, so rows' orders can add up to more than All's. Notes: "Left out: {n} voided sale(s), {amount}; {m} bill(s) cancelled." and one of: lines — "Each line as it was sold, its add-ons with it, so the products, the categories and the sizes add up to the sales. The margin is what they came to less the cost of what they used; kept, less what refunds gave back and the cost they put back."; add-ons — "Each add-on as it was sold on its line, its share of the discount taken off. Refunds are not taken off here."; payments — "What each way of paying took of the sales, and what their refunds gave back that way. A payment pays for a whole sale, so payments go with the hour, the day, the person, the channel and the branch."

summary: The seven days to a day (today unless another is chosen) against the seven before them: net sales day by day, the margin, the orders, what was lost, what sold the most and what rose and fell, each with what changed in words.

title: The month at a glance

title: Menu matrix
summary: Every product sold in the last 4 weeks (or 3 months), placed by how many sold against what each one earns after its cost, in four groups — Keep, Raise the price, Show it more, Change it or drop it — each with what to do.

who.role: owner, general_manager, branch_manager, accountant, auditor, purchasing
who.can: Read it. Someone who works at one place sees their place.

get_there: Reports → Menu matrix: what to keep, reprice, show more or drop →.
before: Products need recipes with costs: a product sold with no cost is left out and named at the bottom.
At least two products with a cost must have sold in the period.

parts.name: Heading and choices
parts.shows: "Menu matrix", Print or save as PDF, and "What each product sells against what it earns on each one, {from} to {to}".

controls.label: Print or save as PDF
controls.does: Prints or saves as PDF.

controls.label: The last 4 weeks
controls.does: 28 days to today (default).

controls.label: The last 3 months
controls.does: 91 days to today.

controls.label: The whole menu
controls.does: Every category together (default).

controls.label: (a category name)
controls.does: Only that category, so like is compared with like (a coffee with coffees).

parts.name: What it says
parts.shows: Sentences: see Messages.

parts.name: Sold against what each one earns (chart)
parts.shows: Each product a mark: across, "Sold in the period"; up, "Earns on each one (IQD)". A line at "Sells a lot from {n} sold" and one at "The menu's average: {amount} on each one" split it into the four groups. Under it: "A product sells a lot when it sold at least {n} in the period: 70% of an even share of the {total} items sold. It earns well when it keeps at least {amount} on each one after its cost: the menu's average. Refunds are taken off." Earns on each = margin kept (after refunds and their cost back) ÷ items sold; the menu's average = all margin kept ÷ all items sold.

controls.label: (a product's mark)
controls.does: Hover or tap to see its name, group, "{n} sold" and "earns {amount} on each"; tap again to hide.

parts.name: The four groups
parts.shows: In the chart's order: Show it more ("Earns well on each one, but few buy it." — "Show it more: first on the menu, a favourite on the till, or offered to customers."), Keep ("Sells a lot and earns well on each one." — "Keep it as it is, first on the menu and among the till's favourites."), Change it or drop it ("Sells little and earns little on each one." — "Change its recipe or price, or take it off the menu."), Raise the price ("Sells a lot, but earns little on each one." — "Raise its price a little, or make it cost less to make."). Each with how many, and a table: Product, Items sold ("{n} · {share}%"), Earns on each, and for Raise the price: Raise by about (what each would need to earn the menu's average, rounded up to 250 IQD). "None in this period." when empty.

states.looks: "Not enough sold yet to compare." with "The matrix compares at least two products sold in the period, each with a cost on its recipe."
At the bottom: "Left out, sold with no cost to judge them by (add their recipe and its costs on Products & Recipes): {list}."

messages.when: Products in Raise the price. Under it: "At the raises shown, as many sold as in this period would bring about {amount} more."
messages.do: Change their prices on Products & Recipes, or lower what they cost to make.

messages.text: Show {n} product(s) more: each earns well, but few are sold.
messages.when: Products in Show it more.
messages.do: Put them first on the menu and the till's favourites; offer them.

messages.text: Change or drop {n} product(s): few are sold, and each earns little.
messages.when: Products in Change it or drop it.
messages.do: Change the recipe or price, or take them off the menu.

messages.text: Keep {n} product(s) first: many are sold, and each earns well.
messages.when: Products in Keep.

messages.text: Left out, sold with no cost to judge them by (add their recipe and its costs on Products & Recipes): {list}.
messages.when: Some products sold had no cost.
messages.do: Give them a recipe with costs.

title: Price watch
summary: What came in dearer in the last 30 days — each item's latest delivery against the one before, by 5% or more — and what it does to the margin of every size that uses it, with the price that keeps the margin, set in one tap.

who.can: Read it and set the price that keeps the margin (Set it).
Read it.

get_there: Reports → Price watch: what came in dearer →.
before: Deliveries recorded on Purchasing / Inventory, with their prices; products with recipes and prices.

parts.name: Heading
parts.shows: "Price watch", Print or save as PDF, and "Deliveries of the last 30 day(s), each against the one before". Always the whole café.

controls.label: Print or save as PDF
controls.does: Prints or saves as PDF.

parts.name: Tiles
parts.shows: Came in dearer: how many items ("{n} item(s), by 5% or more"). What it comes to a month: the extra all rises add over a month at the last 30 days' sales ("At the last 30 days' sales"). Sizes it touches: how many sizes use a dearer item ("{n} price(s) would keep the margin").

parts.name: Each item that came in dearer
parts.shows: Most costly first. The item's name and "▲ {pct}%". "{was} → {now} a {unit}, delivered {when}" and the supplier (per kg or L for items kept in g or ml; freight shared in). "At the last 30 days' sales, it comes to about {amount} a month." Then every size it touches, on its recipe or through what is made from it (milk in a base, the base in a gelato), up to 15: What it touches (product · size), Channel, Price, "Margin, before → after" (the after in warning colour when it falls 2 points or more), Adds a serving (the extra cost of one serving), Sold in 30 days, Keeps the margin (the price that keeps the old margin %, rounded up to 250 IQD; "—" when less than half a step above today's price). "And {n} more, each adding less." when more than 15. Or: "No product uses it on its recipe, nor through what is made from it." Footnote: "Each delivery against the one before it, a unit at a time, with freight shared out. A serving costs what a sale would post, with this item at its old price, then its new, once what was bought dearer is what is sold. The price that keeps the margin is rounded up to 250 IQD."

controls.label: Set it
controls.does: Sets that size's price on that channel to the price shown, from today, for every branch. The cell then says "Set from today".
controls.rules: Shown only beside a price that keeps the margin. Its spoken name: "Set the price to {price}".
controls.after: The till sells at the new price from today (a branch with its own price keeps its own). Past sales keep their price. The audit trail records the price change (was and now). Menu screens refresh.

controls.label: Its deliveries and prices →
controls.does: Opens the item on Inventory.

states.looks: "Nothing came in dearer in the last 30 day(s)." with "Each delivery is set against the one before it, item by item."
"Set from today" in place of the Set it button.

messages.text: Set from today
messages.when: Set it worked.
messages.do: Nothing; check the new price on Products & Recipes.

messages.text: A price cannot start in the past: every sale keeps the price it was made at
messages.when: The page was opened yesterday and Set it pressed after midnight.
messages.do: Reload the page and press Set it again.

messages.text: Unknown product
messages.when: The size was removed meanwhile.

messages.text: Still no answer. It may have been saved: press the same button again to check. It will not be recorded twice.
messages.when: No answer from the server after the retries.
messages.do: Press Set it again; it will not be set twice.

messages.text: You do not have permission to do this (needs recipe.edit)
messages.when: The person's menu permission was removed while the page was open.

messages.text: This screen could not be loaded
messages.when: The deliveries could not be read.

skipped_messages: set_price "Enter a price", "Choose one of the café's branches", "Price must be a number greater than zero": the button always sends a price above zero and no branch.
Retry-key messages (badKey, idem_begin): the screen always sends a key.

what_if.case: The rise was a one-off
what_if.do: Do not change the price; the next delivery will show whether it lasts.

what_if.case: You want a different price than the one shown
what_if.do: Set it on Products & Recipes instead.

tips: The month figure uses the last 30 days' sales: a product sold a lot matters more than a big rise on something rarely sold.
